# HarnessDock v0.2.1

This corrected Tauri 2 release supersedes the incomplete v0.2.0 publication path.

## Key fixes

- Windows x64 ships and resolves Windows-native runtime dependencies only. The retained thin resolver honors npm `os`/`cpu` constraints before downloading, so Windows does not fetch Linux-only native packages.
- Thin first-launch download progress uses the real package completion percentage, while metadata/startup phases are indeterminate instead of showing synthetic progress.
- Thin splash uses the real HarnessDock icon with fixed DPI-safe dimensions and a stable progress layout.
- Desktop startup now includes plugin compatibility recovery in both Tauri and the retained packaged thin path. A complete user profile is always attempted first. Only after a real startup failure does HarnessDock run boot-free `dsh --dump-config`, identify third-party/user-added rows, temporarily disable the row(s) implicated by the failure (or external rows when diagnostics are ambiguous), and retry once.
- Recovery never rewrites `cordis.patch.yml` or `$DSH_HOME`; it is session-only. Official `@deepseek-ai/*` rows and HarnessDock's `embedded-client` bridge are excluded from fallback isolation. Tauri exposes the isolated row IDs as a degraded-but-running state.
- `HARNESSDOCK_PLUGIN_RECOVERY=0` disables the compatibility retry for debugging.
- Linux runtime is glibc-only and removes musl-native variants before AppImage/deb packaging.
- DeepSeek Harness remains pinned to `dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.1` / `cd5ef8148158c3a752a658978873241fdf8e2bbc`.

## Public platform assets

The public v0.2.1 assets are Tauri-native; legacy Electron installers are not published as v0.2.1 assets.

- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-windows-x64-setup.exe`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-linux-x64.deb`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-linux-x64.AppImage`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-macos-x64.dmg`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-macos-arm64.dmg`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-android-arm64-debug.apk`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-android-arm64-debug.aab`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-ios-arm64-simulator.zip`
- Four platform-specific pinned runtime bundles
- `SHA256SUMS`

## Release gate

Publication requires the complete `tauri-candidate` matrix from the exact current `main` SHA: Windows NSIS, Linux deb/AppImage, macOS x64/arm64 DMG, Android APK/AAB, iOS simulator archive, four runtime bundles, runtime smoke checks, TypeScript tests on Windows/Linux/macOS, Rust Tauri recovery tests, and version consistency checks. The publisher refuses stale candidates and refuses to overwrite an existing v0.2.1 tag/release.

## Signing

Public CI packages are build-verified but are not currently Authenticode-signed, Apple-notarized, Google Play-signed, or App Store/TestFlight-provisioned.
